The selected area electron diffraction pattern (SAED) from the [001] direction of the inter-dendritic region (inset of Fig. 1(b)) shows the presence of super-lattice reflections corresponding to L1 2 ordered structure along with fundamental fcc reflections.

The centred dark-field image recorded with the {100} super-lattice reflection (Fig. 1(d)) shows spheroidal γ′ precipitates of size (<r>) 28 ± 7 nm that are distributed uniformly within the matrix. The higher magnification dark-field image in inset of Fig. 1(d) shows, in addition, the presence of fine irregular shaped bright γ′ precipitates within the γ matrix.

The secondary electron SEM micrograph of the HEACoNi alloy subjected to heat-treatment at 900 °C for 50 h in Fig. 2(b) shows a uniform distribution of cuboidal precipitates with rounded corners within the γ-matrix, as can also be easily seen in a high magnification image in the inset of Fig. 2(b).
The DF image clearly reveals cuboidal shape of the bright γ′ precipitates with rounded-corner embedded in the dark γ matrix.
Fig. 1 (a) depicts the secondary electron SEM micrograph of the cast alloy that reveals dendritic and inter-dendritic regions with solute segregation in the inter-dendritic region
The grain sizes of the alloy under solutionized condition vary in the range of 100 to 250 µm.

evidence.section: 4.1 The evolution of microstructure in the two-phase high entropy alloy
evidence.quote: Solutionising heat-treatment at 1250 °C for 25h followed by water quenching could not suppress the formation of fine γ′ precipitates which now appear with bimodal size distribution.
The hardness value increases from the solutionized condition of 330 ± 8 (HV) to a peak value of 380 ± 5 (HV) after 50 h of aging and remains stable thereafter.
The hardness value increases from the solutionized condition of 330 ± 8 (HV) to a peak value of 380 ± 5 (HV) after 50 h of aging and remains stable thereafter.
YS of the HEACoNi alloy initially decreases from room temperature value (25 °C) of 770 MPa to 674 MPa at 670 °C.
YS of the HEACoNi alloy initially decreases from room temperature value (25 °C) of 770 MPa to 674 MPa at 670 °C.
However, beyond 670 °C, a positive temperature dependence of YS is observed with a peak strength value of 772 MPa at 770 °C.
Further increase in temperature to 970 °C decreases strength to 465 MPa.
The heating cycle shows the γ′ solvus temperature of 1156 °C, which represents highest reported solvus temperature amongst the precipitation hardened high entropy alloys.
